editorial:
Ever wondered what a Greek tragedy would look like if it happened in a modern theater setting? You get to see the story of Oedipus, the king of Thebes, but with a really cool twist. The movie takes place in the dressing rooms of a theater where a group of actors is getting ready to perform. The most special part is that the cast is made up of actors with disabilities. This gives the whole movie a very raw and honest feeling. You aren't just watching a play; you are watching the people behind the roles deal with a heavy story about fate and family secrets. It feels more like a personal journey than a stiff history lesson, making the old story feel fresh and real for you.

What really stands out is the acting. The performers bring so much heart to their roles that you forget you are watching a re-telling of an old myth. The pacing is steady, and while it is a drama, it never feels boring because you are curious about how it all ends. If you like movies that focus on human emotions and unique perspectives, you will love this. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend when you want something that makes you think.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the truth finally comes out. You see that Oedipus accidentally killed his father and married his mother, just like the old legend says. Unable to handle the shock and the guilt of what he did, he blinds himself. The movie wraps up by showing the sadness of his fall from power. It ends with a feeling of deep loss, leaving you to think about how no one can run away from their destiny.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves unique indie films and powerful human stories.
